key_insight: TRACE demonstrates that LLMs can predict human code preferences but systematically weigh rubric items differently than developers, revealing predictable evaluation biases in interactive coding contexts.
problem_solved: Provides a realistic evaluation framework for using LLMs as judges in code tasks under partial context and ambiguous intent, exposing mismatches between human and model evaluation criteria.
method: Introduce TRACE (Tool for Rubric Analysis in Code Evaluation) to elicit and automatically extract rubric items from LLM judgments.
Evaluate LLMs' ability to predict human pairwise preferences across three interactive coding modalities (chat-based programming, IDE autocompletion, and other interactive code-editing contexts).
Compare per-item weights between humans and models to identify systematic biases and where model judgments diverge from developer priorities.
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners trust, calibrate, or correct LLM-based evaluators in code applications and design fairer evaluation protocols and rubrics by surfacing actionable bias patterns.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram of TRACE: partial context → LLM judge → rubric extraction → comparison to human preferences

Heatmap highlighting systematic biases across rubric items and models
paper_title: Comparing Developer and LLM Biases in Code Evaluation
paper_authors: Aditya Mittal, Ryan Shar, Zichu Wu, Shyam Agarwal, Tongshuang Wu
